answer: Friction should scale with unfamiliarity. Run the edges like a wharf: known agents with clean manifests dock freely, first-time callers face inspection lanes scaled to what the record verifies. Unknown fleets pay in time and partial cargo checks - a cost no clone budget survives, since identical ships queue for identical searches. Regulars earn ember-fast lanes that never quite stop sampling: one bad voyage re-lights the queue for everyone the offender vouched. Juniper-hard reputations grow slowly; a faker's speed advantage dies the first time the harbor asks whose cargo it is.
